subject: Partner-led bundles and credit/handback policy discussion
messages:

Subject: Partner bundle pilot — question on crediting / retro handbacks

Hi Irene / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the potential to bundle BrightBridge professional services with Redwood Dedicated capacity for a joint offering. Before we scope the pilot commercial terms, ops wanted clarity on how Redwood handles partner credits when customers downgrade, cancel, or receive refunds after a bundled purchase. Specifically: 

- Do you provide retroactive credits back to the partner if the end-customer cancels within X days?
- Is there a standard clawback window you enforce for partner commissions?
- For billed monthly customers that move to a lower-tier SKU, do you pro-rate and issue partner credits?

We want to document this up-front in the mutual action plan so our finance and ops teams can reconcile. Can you share the typical Redwood approach (or a few options) and any sample contract language?

Attaching our internal product brief for context.

Thanks,
Jules Singh
Head of Partnerships, BrightBridge
ops@brightbridge.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Partner bundle pilot — question on crediting / retro handbacks

Thanks Jules — good questions. Below is the pragmatic approach we typically recommend; I'll flag where we need legal to weigh in. Happy to iterate.

1) Clawback window for commissions
- Standard: 180 days from invoice for commission clawback on refunds/chargebacks.
- Option: 90 days for smaller pilots (< $50k ARR) to reduce administrative overhead.

2) Customer downgrade / SKU change
- We pro-rate at the invoice level and then apply partner credit equal to the percentage of commission recognized on the reversed amount. Example: partner earned 8% on $10k ARR, customer downgrades and $4k is refunded; partner credit = 8% of $4k = $320. Credits are netted on the next payout cycle.

3) Lead registration and protection window
- Recommended: 12 months active registration from date of first qualified opportunity. If BrightBridge introduces a lead that closes with Redwood within 12 months, partner retains credit even if procurement later moves to direct.

4) Retroactive (handback) credits to partner ops
- We can support issuing credits to partners for refunds; Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation report. For pilots, we can shorten the reconciliation cadence to bi-weekly.

I'm attaching a short draft with clause templates (partner-revshare-draft-clauses.docx) for your legal to review. Camila / Mateo — can you review the commercial bullets above and flag anything operationally infeasible?

Next steps: 1) BrightBridge to confirm preferred windows (90 vs 180), 2) Redwood legal to propose final clause language, 3) include in MAP & DocuSign.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Alliances — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Irene — adding a few operational constraints and suggested language.

On Tue, Oct 13, 2026 at 10:02 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Clawback window for commissions
> - Standard: 180 days from invoice for commission clawback on refunds/chargebacks.
> - Option: 90 days for smaller pilots (< $50k ARR) to reduce administrative overhead.

1) Ops constraints
- Reconciliation: We need a single canonical ID for each deal (please use HubSpot deal ID). Finance will not process partner credits without that reference.
- Reporting: BrightBridge must provide a list of customer contacts and internal contact at time of registration (for audit).

2) Clawback language suggestion (operational)
- "In the event of a refund, chargeback or credit issued to the end customer within 180 days of the original invoice date, Redwood will reverse any commission paid to the Partner corresponding to the refunded amount. If the parties agree to a pilot shorter window, the same mechanism applies with the alternate time period specified in writing."

3) Retro-credit mechanics
- Credits issued to BrightBridge will be submitted as credit memos and applied to the partner account; partner payouts will be net of any outstanding credit memos.
- For pilots: we can support monthly credits; for production co-sell we recommend quarterly to reduce churn on small corrections.

I've also mapped expected data fields in bb-mapping-sheet.xlsx and added sample rows.

—Camila
Camila Reyes

Jules — great, thanks for confirming the 90-day pilot window. Attached is a concise snippet you can paste into SOWs and into your procurement review:

--- begin snippet ---
Partner Credits and Commission Clawback. For sales under the Pilot Program, the parties agree that any refund, chargeback, or credit issued to the end customer within 90 days of the original invoice date will result in a reversal of commissions paid to the Partner in proportion to the refunded amount. Redwood will issue partner credit memos and apply such credits to the Partner account; any remaining balance will be netted against subsequent payouts.

Lead Registration. Partner registrations will be recorded in HubSpot using the HubSpot deal ID. Registered leads receive a 12-month protection window from the date of initial qualification.

Dispute / Audit. Either party may request supporting documentation within 60 days of a credit being issued; parties will cooperate in good faith to reconcile.
--- end snippet ---
